Separating batches from stock items is important because different deliveries of the same ingredient may have different expiry or availability conditions.</w:t></w:r></w:p>

paragraphs.text: Figure 8 defines JAPZInventoryProfile, a UML documentation profile intended to label inventory-specific elements consistently. Its InventoryRecord stereotype extends a UML Class and introduces properties for the base unit and whether audit fields are used. The interaction begins when a staff member enters delivery data in the Receiving UI. The UI sends the delivery information and a request identifier to the API/Service. The top-level requirement, INV-00 Inventory Management, states that the system should support accurate and controlled stock operations. The deriveReqt relationships show how this broad objective is broken down into requirements that can be associated with implementation responsibilities. INV-01, Access Control, limits stock-changing operations to approved Inventory or Admin users and is satisfied by Access Middleware. INV-02, Reliable Receiving, requires related receiving records to be committed together and repeated requests not to duplicate stock; Stock Receiving Service is identified as the responsible component.</w:t></w:r></w:p>

The satisfy relationships make each requirement traceable to a named implementation element.
